Alphabet Stumbles, U.S. Economy Surges
 
Plus, DoorDash to buy Instacart and ServiceNow shares tank
 
By Heard on the Street Staff
 
 
GINA M RANDAZZO/ZUMA PRESS
 

This is an edition of the Markets P.M. newsletter, a recap of the day’s most important markets moves, delivered after the closing bell. If you’re not subscribed, sign up here.

 
 
 

What Happened in Markets Today

 

Alphabet shares fell 13%, after the Google parent’s disappointing quarterly update late Wednesday. Revenue from its core search unit fell short, due partly to the popularity of less-profitable “AI mode” searches. The company also burned cash at a faster rate than expected. Alphabet’s market value declined by about half a trillion dollars and helped drag the Nasdaq down 1.4% on the day. The S&P 500 dropped 0.3%. The Dow industrials declined 0.3%, hurt by a revenue miss at Caterpillar, which lost 9%.

 

U.S. economic growth accelerated over the summer. The Commerce Department said U.S. gross domestic product rose at a 3.4% annual rate in the third quarter, adjusted for inflation and seasonality. It was the fastest pace in a year and beat analysts’ expectations of 3.1%. This was the last major report on the U.S. economy before Tuesday’s midterm elections.

 

DoorDash agreed to buy Instacart for $17 billion, expanding its reach into grocery delivery. The deal values Instacart at about a 26% premium to its closing price Oct. 22 before news reports that it was pursuing a sale.

 

ADT agreed to be acquired by Josh Kushner’s Thrive. The home-security company, based in Boca Raton, Fla., said Thrive would pay $10 a share in cash, a 35% premium to Wednesday’s closing price.

 

ServiceNow shares plunged 27%, the S&P 500’s biggest decliner. The software maker’s earnings report pointed to decelerating revenue growth over the next 12 months. Shares of Fortinet, a cybersecurity company, lost 20% after its earnings report raised concerns about declining sales momentum.
